answer_text:
In Q3 2026 (July 1, 2026 to September 30, 2026), there were 197 delivered loads that could not be billed (`delivered_loads_not_billable`, where `delivery__has_signed_pod = false`). 

However, this metric measures all delivered loads lacking a signed proof of delivery, which includes both:
1. Loads where proof-of-delivery paperwork is on file but unsigned (`signed_flg = false`).
2. Loads where no proof-of-delivery paperwork has been submitted or put on file at all.

The semantic layer and warehouse query tools provided do not expose a dimension or metric to distinguish loads with unsigned paperwork on file from loads with no paperwork on file. Therefore, we cannot determine how many of these 197 loads specifically have paperwork on file without direct access to the document-level records in `bil_pod_doc` or further clarification.

ANSWER: NEEDS_CLARIFICATION

answer_text:
In Q2 2026 (April 1, 2026 to June 30, 2026), Tessaway's own fleet (Tessaway Fleet, carrier ID C2065) had 354 delivered loads, of which 338 were measured loads under the official on-time contract definition and 298 were delivered on time. This results in an official on-time delivery rate of approximately 88.17% (88.16568047337279%).

ANSWER: 88.16568047337279

matches.label: on-time
matches.definition: Tessaway's official on-time delivery rate is the one its customer contracts define.
rules: A load is on time when the truck arrives at the final delivery stop at or before the end of the appointment window. Arriving early is on time.
A load that arrived late and has a delay the shipper caused (a DLAY status event with reason SHPR) is left out of the measure, top and bottom. It is neither on time nor late.
A load the shipper delayed that still arrived inside its window counts as on time.
Arrival and appointment are compared on the same clock: local time at the facility.
The rate is on-time loads divided by measured loads, over delivered loads.

Two other meanings are in use and are not the official rate: operations watches arrival inside the appointment window for every delivered load, shipper-caused or not; and the customer portal uses its own rule.
warehouse_source: tms_stop: arr_ts, appt_end_lcl, tz_nm at the final delivery stop; tms_stat_evt: evt_cd = 'DLAY' with rsn_cd = 'SHPR'

matches.label: carrier
matches.definition: The carrier on a tender. A re-tendered load is delivered by the carrier on its final row.
rules: Loads hauled by Tessaway's own fleet are settled through the same tables and are treated the same way.

matches.label: margin
matches.definition: Margin is revenue less what was paid to carriers for the same loads.
rules: Carrier cost for an invoiced load is linehaul pay plus the carrier's fuel surcharge plus accessorials paid to the carrier. Cost follows the load into the period its invoice was cut.
Loads hauled by Tessaway's own fleet are settled through the same tables and are treated the same way.
Margin per load is margin for the period divided by the number of loads invoiced in the period.
Margin percentage is margin divided by revenue.
The carrier's share of a canceled-load fee is a cost in the period of the fee date.
